describe.reach-search: Agent Reach: semantic web search (Exa) and search tools — find sources on any topic before reading them.

describe.reach-video: Agent Reach: videos and podcasts — YouTube and Bilibili subtitles/transcripts, podcast transcription.
describe.reach-web: Agent Reach: read any web page or RSS feed as clean text (Jina Reader and fallbacks).
describe.reach-dev: Agent Reach: developer sources — GitHub repos, issues, PRs and code search through the gh CLI.
describe.reach-career: Agent Reach: jobs and recruiting — LinkedIn and Boss Zhipin profiles and job listings.
describe.reach-finance: Agent Reach: market data — stock quotes and discussions (Xueqiu) for research.

items.name: cs-grade
items.description: Phase 3 — the bounded grade→iterate loop. Define a CMA outcome (required rubric, max_iterations 1..20), read each grader verdict, decide the next move, and run held-back eval cases once a version passes, via the grade-iterate skill. Never unbounded.

items.description: Main entry / resume for building a Claude Managed Agent. Runs the agent-launcher-orchestrator skill from the current session goal — reads ./my-agent/goal.json, routes to the right phase (interview → stage-launch → grade-iterate → run-without-you → wrap-up), compiles the loop/workflow, and forks to the phase skill. Emits BYOK curl; never makes API calls or prints the key.

items.name: cs-run-without-you

Turn a graded agent into a recurring POSIX-cron scheduled deployment (optionally self-grading each firing), an event-driven curl trigger, or on-demand use, then finalize NEXT-DIRECTIONS, via the run-without-you skill. Tests with a manual run before trusting the schedule.

Select and classify endpoints, estimate sample size / power (means / proportions / survival), and score a study plan for a GO / GO-WITH-CONDITIONS / REDESIGN / NO-GO phase-gate decision. Every output is an ESTIMATE plus a named clinical owner — never clinical fact. Direct invocation of the clinical-research skill.

items.name: cs-grill-research-ops
items.description: Matt Pocock-style docs-anchored grilling for a Research Operations plan — clinical study, R&D budget, market size, or product study. Walks the plan against the research canon (ICH E9, IAS 38, Cochran, Kotler, Nielsen) one question at a time, recommends an answer per question, and refuses to invoke any sub-skill until the lane-defining decisions are locked. Use before running /cs:research-ops on a fuzzy plan.

items.name: cs-market-research
items.description: Market research methodology. Size a market as TAM/SAM/SOM computed BOTH top-down and bottoms-up (never a single number), plan a survey sample size with finite-population correction and per-segment minimums, and score candidate segments against Kotler's criteria. Outputs always show method + assumptions. Direct invocation of the market-research skill.

items.name: cs-product-research
items.description: Product / user research methodology. Select the right method for the goal (generative vs evaluative vs validation), compute method-based saturation / sample size with an explicit confidence level, and synthesize coded observations into insights while flagging single-source anecdotes. Never fabricates insight. Direct invocation of the product-research skill.

items.name: cs-research-finance
items.description: R&D program finance. Build a multi-period program budget with the F&A (indirect) split, track burn rate and runway against value-inflection milestones, and route R&D cost items to a capitalize-vs-expense determination. Every budget surfaces its assumptions; capex-vs-opex routes to a named finance owner and never auto-decides. Direct invocation of the research-finance skill.

items.name: cs-research-ops
items.description: Top-level Research Operations router. Classifies an enterprise research inquiry (clinical study design / R&D finance / market research / product research) and forks context to the right sub-skill via the research-ops-skills orchestrator, returning a ≤200-word digest with a named owner and one grill challenge.

items.name: 01-intro-to-ai-agents
items.title: Introduction to AI Agents and Agent Use Cases
items.description: Welcome to the **AI Agents for Beginners** course! This course gives you the foundational knowledge — and real working code — to start building AI Agents from scratch.

items.name: 02-explore-agentic-frameworks
items.title: Explore AI Agent Frameworks
items.description: AI agent frameworks are software platforms designed to simplify the creation, deployment, and management of AI agents. These frameworks provide developers with pre-built components, abstractions, and tools that streamline the development of complex AI systems.

items.title: AI Agentic Design Principles
items.description: There are many ways to think about building AI Agentic Systems. Given that ambiguity is a feature and not a bug in Generative AI design, it’s sometimes difficult for engineers to figure out where to even start. We have created a set of human-centric UX Design Principles to enable developers to build customer-centric agentic systems to solve their business needs. These design principles are not a prescriptive archite…

items.name: 04-tool-use
items.title: Tool Use Design Pattern
items.description: Tools are interesting because they allow AI agents to have a broader range of capabilities. Instead of the agent having a limited set of actions it can perform, by adding a tool, the agent can now perform a wide range of actions. In this chapter, we will look at the Tool Use Design Pattern, which describes how AI agents can use specific tools to achieve their goals.

items.name: 05-agentic-rag
items.title: Agentic RAG
items.description: This lesson provides a comprehensive overview of Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Agentic RAG), an emerging AI paradigm where large language models (LLMs) autonomously plan their next steps while pulling information from external sources. items.name: 06-building-trustworthy-agents

items.description: This lesson will cover: How to build and deploy safe and effective AI Agents; Important security considerations when developing AI Agents.; How to maintain data and user privacy when developing AI Agents.

items.name: 07-planning-design
items.title: Planning Design
items.description: This lesson will cover

items.name: 08-multi-agent

items.description: As soon as you start working on a project that involves multiple agents, you will need to consider the multi-agent design pattern. However, it might not be immediately clear when to switch to multi-agents and what the advantages are.

items.name: 09-metacognition
items.title: Metacognition in AI Agents
items.description: Welcome to the lesson on metacognition in AI agents! This chapter is designed for beginners who are curious about how AI agents can think about their own thinking processes. By the end of this lesson, you'll understand key concepts and be equipped with practical examples to apply metacognition in AI agent design.

items.name: 10-ai-agents-production

items.description: As AI agents move from experimental prototypes to real-world applications, the ability to understand their behavior, monitor their performance, and systematically evaluate their outputs becomes important.

items.description: As the use of AI agents grows, so does the need for protocols that ensure standardization, security, and support open innovation. In this lesson, we will cover 3 protocols looking to meet this need - Model Context Protocol (MCP), Agent to Agent (A2A) and Natural Language Web (NLWeb).

items.name: 16-deploying-scalable-agents

items.name: containerization
items.title: Run Pi in an isolated environment
items.description: Use an isolated environment to limit the files, credentials, processes, and network services that generated commands can access or affect.

items.name: extensions
items.title: Extensions
items.description: Extensions are TypeScript modules that add executable behavior to Pi. Use one when a workflow needs tools, commands, event handlers, model providers, session state, or terminal UI rather than instructions alone.

items.name: how-pi-works
items.title: How Pi Works
items.description: Pi coordinates model requests, tool execution, context assembly, and session storage. A session is Pi's record of a conversation, including messages, tool calls and results, model changes, compactions, and other events.

items.name: mcp
items.title: MCP Servers
items.description: Pi connects to [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) servers over stdio or streamable HTTP and makes their tools available to the model.

items.name: prompt-templates
items.title: Prompt Templates
items.description: Prompt templates turn Markdown files into reusable `/` commands. Use one when you want to reuse the same prompt without adding executable behavior or a larger set of supporting instructions.

items.name: sdk
items.title: SDK
items.description: `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` embeds Pi in a Node.js or Bun process. It provides direct TypeScript access to the agent, sessions, tools, models, and resources used by the command-line application.

items.name: security
items.title: Run Pi safely
items.description: Treat model-generated commands and code as untrusted. Pi can read, change, and execute files with the permissions of the account that started it, and it does not ask for approval before every tool call. Extensions, package installers, language servers, and other child processes run with those same permissions unless an operating-system or virtualization boundary restricts them.

items.name: sessions
items.title: Sessions and Context
items.description: Pi saves a conversation as a session. The active branch of that session supplies conversation history for the next model request. Use session commands to continue work, explore another branch, or reduce the amount of history sent to the model.

items.name: skills
items.title: Skills
items.description: Skills give Pi specialized instructions and supporting files for a particular kind of work. Pi advertises each available skill by name and description, then loads its full instructions only when the task calls for them.

items.name: reach-scout
